findings.passage: I have worked to ensure that voter integrity is in place by passing a Voter ID law to ensure that only citizens that are eligible to vote may exercise that right. I assisted in passing a law that placed stringent requirements on the NC State Board of Elections to clean up the voter rolls and remove duplicate registrations as well as any deceased individuals.
findings.note: From his 2024 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers (campaign key messages). He describes the state photo ID law and voter-roll clean-up legislation as work he took part in.

findings.passage: Election integrity is a major concern. We must ensure that only citizens are allowed to vote in our elections. Voter I.D. and signature verification must be implemented to ensure that outside interference does not occur.
findings.note: From his 2022 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers (campaign key messages, written as a candidate).

findings.passage: We must ensure that our elections are free and fair and that the electoral process is available to only our citizens through voter I.D. and signature verification on ballots without interference from outside entities.
findings.note: Same 2022 survey, answer on policy areas he cares about.

Co-sponsor of HB 825, Election Improvements (filed 4/8/2025; sent to House Rules and not acted on). Among other things it would require the last four digits of the Social Security number plus a driver license, state ID card or date of birth number on absentee ballot requests, and set an alternative affidavit for voters who cannot attach an ID copy.

Co-sponsor of HB 958, Election Law Changes. The ratified text requires a county board to process a registration application only if it states the applicant is a U.S. citizen, with a sworn citizenship form if the answer is blank, and sets a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database. The bill page also shows a Governor's veto entry.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (RCS 758, 66-47)
findings.note: Voted aye on second reading of HB 958 (citizenship on registration, non-citizen removal, other election changes) per his member votes page.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, M11 Concur (RCS 801, 62-47)
findings.note: Voted aye on the House concurrence vote on HB 958 per his member votes page.

Primary sponsor of HB 1231, No Voter Registration Changes At DMV (filed 5/11/2026; sent to House Rules). It would require voters to make address, name or affiliation changes at county boards of elections instead of at DMV, and keeps the DMV question asking if the applicant is a U.S. citizen.
